articles.title: Monsoon Session Sees Passage of Three Key Bills
articles.summary: Parliament wrapped up its monsoon session with the passage of the Digital India Bill, an amendment to the Representation of the People Act, and a new framework for federal-state fiscal transfers. The Digital India Bill introduces data-protection duties for platforms and creates a new grievance-redressal authority. The RP Act amendment tightens disclosure rules for candidates.

articles.title: Supreme Court Reaffirms Basic Structure Doctrine
articles.summary: In a five-judge constitution bench ruling, the Supreme Court reaffirmed that Parliament cannot amend the basic structure of the Constitution. The judgment strikes down an amendment that would have curtailed judicial review of certain executive orders. The bench held that judicial review is itself a part of the basic structure.

articles.title: ECI Issues New Guidelines for Social Media Campaigns
articles.summary: The Election Commission of India has released updated guidelines for political campaigning on social media platforms. All political ads must now carry clear disclaimers identifying the sponsor and funding source. AI-generated content depicting real politicians must carry a visible disclosure.

articles.title: Uttarakhand's UCC Enters Second Year of Implementation
articles.summary: Uttarakhand's Uniform Civil Code completed one year of implementation this week. The state government released data showing over 12,000 marriage registrations and 800 live-in relationship declarations under the new law. A constitutional challenge is pending before the Uttarakhand High Court.

articles.title: Panel Set Up to Review 73rd Amendment Implementation
articles.summary: A parliamentary standing committee has been set up to review the working of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment, which created the Panchayati Raj system in 1992. The panel will examine fiscal devolution to panchayats, functional autonomy, and the reservation of seats for women and marginalised communities.
